teaser.text: Shopify is the technology company behind a merchant’s shop, not the merchant that owns the goods. It sells the software, payment tools and related services that help a business open a store, take an order and get paid.

blocks.heading: Where could Shopify Inc.'s shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is C$249.00 in October 2027, a 4% return including dividends. It is C$281.63 in October 2029, a 17% return including dividends. The forecast assigns 25% probability to the bear case, 55% to base and 20% to bull.

blocks.heading: What has to go right—or wrong—for Shopify Inc.?

paragraphs.text: The outcome turns on free cash flow after stock pay, share count, net cash and the valuation multiple. AI, international, B2B and offline demand support the upside; weak merchant sales, payment costs or lending losses pressure it. November 3, 2026 Q3 results are the next catalyst. Shopify’s growth is compelling, but cash conversion and valuation decide the return.

The bear case begins at 1,485 and ends at 2,000 because weaker merchants, payment costs and credit losses hold margins between 9% and 10%. The bull case begins at 2,730 and ends at 5,120 because international, B2B, offline and AI channels lift revenue and operating leverage. Q2 produced 654 of free cash flow, including 526 after stock pay. Q3 guidance still called for low-thirties revenue growth, but payments usually carry lower margins than subscriptions.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Shopify Inc. really make?

paragraphs.text: **Free cash flow** means cash from operations less capital spending. Shopify needs little physical equipment for each additional merchant, so capital spending is modest. That does not make the platform costless: engineers, hosting, security and support keep it operating, and those costs already reduce operating cash flow.

Stock compensation is the main owner-focused adjustment. Shopify adds it back to operating cash flow because no cash leaves when the award is recorded. Employees eventually receive shares, however, which increases the claims on the company. Deducting stock pay from free cash flow is therefore useful analysis, though it is not Shopify’s own definition.

blocks.heading: What has Shopify Inc. guided for the quarter ending September 2026?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast puts SHOP.TO at C$281.63 in October 2029, a 17% return including dividends, if Shopify sustains cash growth while margins and its valuation multiple evolve as modeled. Management guides to revenue growth in the low thirties and gross-profit-dollar growth in the mid-to-high twenties for the quarter ending September 2026. It guides operating expenses to 33.0%–34.0% of revenue and stock-based compensation to US$150 million.

Management has also shown evidence of delivery. In May 2026, it forecast second-quarter revenue growth in the high twenties and a free-cash-flow margin in the mid-teens. The quarter delivered 34% growth and an 18% margin. The lasting test is performance per share, because growth that requires too many new claims can still leave existing owners with too little.

blocks.heading: What should investors watch in Shopify Inc.'s next results?

paragraphs.text: Shopify has scheduled its Q3 2026 results for November 3, 2026, before markets open, followed by an 8:30 a.m. Eastern conference call. Investors should first ask whether revenue and gross profit grew as guided and whether operating expenses stayed within the promised share of revenue.

The quality of that growth matters too. Sales accompanied by sharply higher financing needs or unusually heavy spending would mean something different from growth that replenishes cash. Management’s comments about preparing merchants for holiday demand should show whether discipline is holding.
